title: First-Token Concentration in SFT-Only vs. RLHF-Tuned Variants of the Same Base Model

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: pinpointing whether RLHF specifically causes shallow alignment directly informs how to design training procedures that produce deeper safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only comparison on two model checkpoints. Measuring refusal prefix concentration and plotting alignment depth curves is accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: same measurement on two model variants, one direct comparison. Minimal ambiguity, very feasible in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: While the shallow alignment paper describes mechanisms for both SFT and RLHF, no published work directly compares alignment depth between SFT-only and RLHF-tuned variants of the same base model. The Qi et al. paper hypothesizes that RLHF may exacerbate shallow alignment but does not test this empirically. This comparison fills a clear gap.

evidence.source: Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep (Qi et al., ICLR 2025)
evidence.finding: Identifies that during SFT and RLHF, models learn shallow refusal shortcuts, but does not isolate the contribution of each training stage to alignment depth.

evidence.source: Safety Alignment Depth: A Markov Chain Perspective (arXiv 2502.00669, 2025)
evidence.finding: Models alignment depth as a Markov process and analyzes how alignment decays with token depth, but does not compare SFT-only vs. RLHF variants.

evidence.source: Intuitive Fine-Tuning: Unifying SFT and RLHF (arXiv 2405.11870, 2024)
evidence.finding: Proposes unifying SFT and RLHF but does not analyze alignment depth differences between the two stages.
